title: Craft Source-Preserving Transplant and Rebinding Chain
objective: Copy the current DomainSpec v2 product workspace into CyberAlchemy Lab as Craft, then rename and rebind the copied system dependency-aware without reconstructing its definitions, compiler, runtime, or evidence machinery.

preserved: P0-P2 exact prototype bytes and validation evidence
determinism, hostile-test, rollback, freeze, test, and approval obligations
superseded: continuing P3 as a newly implemented replacement compiler or runtime
materializing the migrated product one definition witness at a time
treating prototype construction as the source of the Craft implementation

construction_rule: Transplant first, rebind second, validate third. Existing source bytes are evidence and implementation material; copied placement grants no admission or authority.

stages.objective: Copy every selected version-controlled DomainSpec v2 product file outside development history into craft/ with relative paths, bytes, and modes preserved.
stages.exit_evidence: The independent transplant validator reports PASS for exact source selection, bytes, modes, destination closure, exclusions, and zero authority.

stages.objective: Inventory every active DomainSpec product name, package ID, command, path, import, generated target, profile, and user-facing label inside craft/ and classify legacy-only occurrences separately.
stages.exit_evidence: Every occurrence has a typed classification, owner, destination form, dependency order, and validation consumer; no replacement is performed in this stage.

stages.objective: Apply the inventory as an exact dependency-ordered rename and rebinding manifest inside craft/, preserving DS-* semantic IDs and explicit historical provenance.
outputs: active Craft names and paths inside craft/
generated views refreshed from canonical machine sources
stages.exit_evidence: No active package, command, compiler, profile, or user-facing current-name field retains DomainSpec except typed legacy/provenance fields, and every changed consumer resolves.

stages.objective: Bind the copied workspace to its exact Node, pnpm, TypeScript, Python, Rust, Lean, container, filesystem, and network profiles; install or restore only missing dependencies under separately bounded platform effects.
stages.exit_evidence: Every required tool and dependency resolves from an exact profile and lock; unavailable optional lanes remain typed residue rather than hidden PASS.

stages.objective: Run the copied system's existing checks plus hostile rename, stale-path, source-drift, generated-view, rollback, and two-run determinism tests from final Craft paths.
stages.exit_evidence: All acceptance-critical selected-workspace checks pass from final paths and no unresolved residue is inflated into PASS.

stages.objective: Bind the validated Craft workspace to Lab Product, authority, capability, context, platform, and evidence records through references and explicit maps without duplicating its implementation or inferring a Bounded Context from placement.
stages.exit_evidence: All cross-plane identities and references close while the Craft implementation has exactly one active home.

stages.objective: Freeze one exact testable Craft candidate and collect complete current product-test evidence over its copied, rebound, and integrated bytes.
stages.exit_evidence: One immutable candidate and its complete current tests are identified; approval is eligible only when every required result is PASS.

stages.objective: Present the exact tested Craft candidate once for approve, revise, reject, defer, or stop.
stages.exit_evidence: The decision binds the exact candidate and current product-test evidence and has product-approval-only effect.

claim_ceiling: This chain makes the source-preserving migration route explicit. It does not admit copied bytes, complete active-name rebinding, prove runtime conformance, approve the Product, activate consumers, delete legacy sources, commit, publish, release, or deploy.
